issues.claim: NLRA: "Section 7 of the NLRA protects concerted activity; surveillance or the impression of surveillance of union or protected activity is an unfair labor practice" - marked confirmed: true, cited to nlrb.gov/about-nlrb/rights-we-protect/the-law/employees/concerted-activity-0
issues.problem: The rule itself is real and correctly stated, but the cited page does not contain it: that page only describes protected concerted activity and that employers cannot discipline or threaten employees for it. Nothing on it addresses surveillance or the impression of surveillance. Presented as confirmed at a source that does not support the surveillance half.
issues.fix: Re-cite to https://www.nlrb.gov/about-nlrb/rights-we-protect/the-law/employees/your-rights-during-union-organizing, which I opened and which states supervisors and managers cannot spy on employees (or make it appear they are doing so) regarding union activity. Keep the concerted-activity page only for the Section 7 point.

issues.claim: NationCam pricing: "camera rental $39/month fixed, $89 PTZ, $139 panoramic"
issues.problem: The page's starting-price block and the style selector do say rent from $39/month (fixed), $89 (PTZ), $139 (panoramic 180), so the figures are right, but the page's own quote builder renders a default 4 MP fixed camera at "rent from $49/month each". Quoting $39 as the flat fixed-camera rental is slightly stronger than the page supports.
issues.fix: Write it as "fixed camera rental from $39/month (quote builder shows a 4 MP fixed camera from $49/month); PTZ from $89; panoramic from $139".

issues.claim: Frigate hardware guidance: "4 GB RAM minimum with a dedicated detector, 8 GB practical, 16 GB for larger systems"
issues.problem: The page says 4 GB is the basic minimum with a dedicated accelerator, 8 GB is the minimum if enrichments (face recognition, LPR, extra models) are used, and 16 GB is recommended for 8+ cameras or heavy enrichments. "8 GB practical" is a paraphrase the page does not use and blurs the enrichment threshold that matters for this pilot (a VLM for exception review is exactly an enrichment).
issues.fix: Restate as "4 GB minimum with a dedicated detector; 8 GB minimum if running enrichments such as a VLM or LPR; 16 GB recommended for 8+ cameras".

issues.claim: IET paper outcome: "Efficient-YOLOv5 harness detector: 97.7% precision, 89.3% recall, 94% mAP", sample "3,300 images"
issues.problem: Not contradicted, but I could not open the cited page: ietresearch.onlinelibrary.wiley.com returned HTTP 403 and the DOAJ record returned 403 too. The precision/recall figures are corroborated by search-index summaries of the same DOI (which also give 3,300 images, 94% mAP and 72 FPS), so the numbers look right, but I could not read them at source and the brief presents them as read first-hand.
issues.fix: Either drop the 94% mAP and 3,300-image details, or add a note that this row was read from a secondary summary because the publisher page blocks direct access - the same treatment already given to the Piza et al. CCTV PDF and the BLS/OSHA pages.

issues.claim: NICB/NER estimate "$300 million to $1 billion per year", year field "estimate cited in 2022 article (underlying NICB/NER data older)"
issues.problem: The dollar range is confirmed verbatim on the US Assure page, but that page carries no visible publication date and cites 2013 NICB theft counts as "the latest year for which these statistics are available", so the "2022 article" attribution is unverified.
issues.fix: Change the year to "undated US Assure article (cites 2013 NICB/NER figures)" and repeat the existing caveat that the vintage is unclear, rather than asserting a 2022 citation date.
